newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo '96 industry growth seen at 7 pct - institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo '96 industry growth seen at 7 pct - institute.

text.p: A leading Belgrade economic institute on Friday raised its forecast for 1996 industrial growth to seven percent from 5.9 because of the sector's successful performance in October.
"Year-on-year industrial production in October registered a significant rise of 12.4 percent," said Miroljub Labus, a senior economist at the Belgrade Economics Institute.
"Despite the fact this is seasonal growth, we expect positive industrial activity to continue and we forecast growth this year of seven percent," he told reporters.
According to official statistics, industrial production in October rose 15.4 percent over September, and rose 6.45 percent in January-October from the same 1995 period.

Labus said the rise in industrial output was due largely to a turnaround in the food sector to an unprecedented 44 percent rise in October after a six percent decline in September, the result of a good harvest.
But he said the economy was unlikely to benefit from the increases because the industrial sector produces few exports.

Labus said the food, energy and chemical sectors accounted for about 80 percent of industrial output, and October's strong performance had made food the leading industrial sector. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4305
